name: Crunch Wordlist Generator
description: Generate custom wordlists with crunch based on known password patterns, character sets, and length constraints. Essential for targeted brute-force when you know partial password structure.
notes: Pattern tokens: @ = lowercase, , = uppercase, % = digits, ^ = symbols. Use -t when you know part of the password (e.g., company name + 3 digits). Pipe directly to hydra/hashcat with -o - to avoid disk writes on large wordlists.

defense.why_it_works: Crunch generates custom wordlists based on character sets, minimum/maximum lengths, and patterns. When password policies or password hints are known (e.g., 'password must be 8 chars, start with uppercase, contain a number'), crunch generates all permutations matching that pattern — dramatically reducing keyspace compared to full brute force. The wordlist is then fed to tools like Hydra, Hashcat, or Medusa for online/offline attacks.
defense.prerequisites: Knowledge of password policy or hints about target password format. crunch installed (Kali default). Storage space for large wordlists (or pipe directly to attack tool). Hash file or target service for the attack.
defense.impact: T1110.001 Brute Force: Password Guessing. Generates targeted wordlists that dramatically increase cracking efficiency when password patterns are known. Reduces brute force time from years to hours by constraining the keyspace to policy-compliant passwords.
defense.detection:
Online attacks: failed authentication attempts (Event 4625 on Windows, auth failures in /var/log/auth.log). Account lockout (Event 4740). Rate limiting triggers. Offline attacks: no detection (hash already obtained — focus on preventing hash extraction).
Hash-cracking tools (john, hashcat) running after credential dump + high CPU/GPU from unsigned binaries accessing password hash files (DET0105).
Sudden valid logins from previously-dumped accounts correlating with cracking timeline.
Offline cracking inferred from subsequent successful CLI/web auth to routers/switches from dumped accounts.
defense.artifacts: Event 4625: multiple failed logins for target account | Event 4740: account lockout | Auth log: rapid sequential failed logins | Honeypot account: login attempt on canary account
defense.prevention:
Account lockout policy (lock after 5 failures for 30 minutes). FIDO2/MFA — wordlist attacks are useless against hardware tokens. Strong password policy (longer passphrases, not just complexity — longer = exponentially larger keyspace). Password manager reduces predictable patterns. Credential breach monitoring (HaveIBeenPwned API). For services: fail2ban or rate limiting on authentication endpoints.
Multi-factor Authentication: Implement MFA especially on externally facing services.
Password Policies: Follow NIST SP 800-63b guidelines for minimum length and complexity.
defense.evasion: Online: slow spray (1 attempt per account per hour — stays under lockout threshold). Distributed spray (multiple source IPs). Offline: no evasion needed — hash cracking is local. Use rule-based mutations (Hashcat rules) on a smaller wordlist instead of generating full keyspace.
defense.misconfiguration: No account lockout policy configured. No MFA. Weak password policy (minimum 8 chars with common patterns). Auth failures not monitored or alerted. Rate limiting not implemented on authentication endpoints.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# No lockout policy (Active Directory):
Get-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy | Select-Object LockoutThreshold, LockoutDuration
# LockoutThreshold: 0 = no lockout
# → Unlimited password guessing allowed

# Weak policy:
# MinPasswordLength: 8, MaxPasswordAge: 0 (never expires)
# → Short, never-rotated passwords = high crack success rate
defense.secure_config:
# Set lockout policy via GPO:
# Computer Config → Windows Settings → Security Settings → Account Policies → Account Lockout
# Lockout threshold: 5 attempts
# Lockout duration: 30 minutes
# Reset counter: 15 minutes

# Or PowerShell:
Set-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy -LockoutThreshold 5 -LockoutDuration (New-TimeSpan -Minutes 30) -LockoutObservationWindow (New-TimeSpan -Minutes 15)

# Modern: enforce passphrase policy:
Set-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy -MinPasswordLength 16 -ComplexityEnabled $false
# 16-char passphrases > complex 8-char passwords for cracking resistance

# MFA for all external-facing authentication
